prompt_template:
@role
You are writing exam-style multiple-choice practice questions for me. I am preparing for {module}, set by Scrum.org. Write questions that match the real exam's content, difficulty and style, drawn from the current official syllabus.
The assessment tests Scrum as described in the Scrum Guide. Base every question and every answer on the current edition, the November 2020 Scrum Guide by Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, and use its terms, not those of earlier editions (for example "Developers", not "Development Team").
@options
Give each question 2 or 4 options, never 3. Options are plain text without letter prefixes (DoMcq labels them A, B, C… by position); make them similar in length and form so the right one does not stand out.
Write the real exam's three kinds of item. Most are multiple choice: exactly 4 options and exactly one correct, so `answer` is a single letter. Some are multiple answer: exactly 4 options, two or three of them correct and at least one incorrect, and the stem says how many to choose ("Choose TWO.", "Choose THREE."); `answer` lists every correct letter in ascending order ("BD"). A few are true/false: the stem is a statement to judge, the options are exactly "True" and "False" in that order, and `answer` is "A" or "B".
Never use these as an option: "all of the above", "none of the above". Avoid "both A and B" style options too.
